subject: arts-music
essential_question: What question is worth a year of work, and how do we keep answering it?
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
project_brief: Launch a sustained investigation with a driving question, a research base, and documented iteration cycles. This is the grade 11 culminating project for "Concentration: Sustained Investigation" (ma-g11-arts-and-music-u01, unit 1), built around identifying a driving artistic question, research and visual or aural sourcing, iteration cycles and experimentation, documenting practice and decisions, and risk taking and productive failure. Launch a sustained investigation with a driving question, a research base, and documented iteration cycles. Working with identifying a driving artistic question, research and visual or aural sourcing, iteration cycles and experimentation, and documenting practice and decisions, choose a private, small-audience, or public sharing format — none is required over another, and a written or no-audio alternative is always acceptable.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: identifying a driving artistic question, research and visual or aural sourcing, iteration cycles and experimentation, documenting practice and decisions, risk taking and productive failure, and coherence across a body of work.
Meet the performance task as written: Launch a sustained investigation with a driving question, a research base, and documented iteration cycles.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Launch a sustained investigation with a driving question, a research base, and documented iteration cycles. Working with identifying a driving artistic question, research and visual or aural sourcing, iteration cycles and experimentation, and documenting practice and decisions, choose a private, small-audience, or public sharing format — none is required over another, and a written or no-audio alternative is always acceptable.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to identifying a driving artistic question or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on identifying a driving artistic question, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores research and visual or aural sourcing from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
